questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: For me the most important thing was finding a destination where I didn't have to worry about money, I could make new friends and still have courses that was relevant for my education. In all these aspects Prague was the ideal destination.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very easy. Prague is used to getting exchange students and are giving you all the information that you need. Furthermore, they have an organization called Erasmus in Prague which is driven by volunteers. They are helping alot, both with accommodation, parties, trips and more.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The faculty of social science had a welcome meeting for exchange students. They gave all the information that you need in the beginning. Before you even arrive, they sent me two documents with relevant information. Furthermore, they have several different what's app groups where you can always ask for the help you need. There is one big group for all exchange studens, one with the organisation Erasmus in Prague, if you live in dorm there is a dorm group and other than this there is running grounp, techno group, football group...

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It isn't exactly on campus. its a dorm but its provided by the university. if you apply for it you will get it. Its possible to make a wish for which dorm you want. make sure to either wish for Hvezda dorm or the dorm in Prague 8. otherwise you can risk getting a dorm in Prague 15, which would mean you have 1 hour of public transportation to the city center.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: In my dorm there is two kitchens per floor. it means 2 kitchens for approximately 80 people. it sounds like nothing but I never had a problem. the kitchen is almost all the time free because all nationalities cook at different hour. for instance the spanish people cook very late in the evening. in the dom in Prague 8, the kitchen is shared between 4 people. so you could take this in to consideration when you apply for the dorm.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Im first gonna explain about my dorm in hvezda. you should be aware that the showers are common showers. they are split between girls and boys. personally I don't mind shower with other people, but I know some people have a problem with this. furthermore you should know that danish people are apparently hygienic compared to many other nationalities. however, there is cleaning in the toilets and shower every morning from monday-friday. You need to clean the room yourself, you can rent a vacuum cleaner for approximately 1,5 kr. so its really cheap. If you live in the dorm in Prague 8, you will share toilet, shower and kitchen with only 3 other people so it might be nicer. they also have way bigger rooms.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I lived on a floor with many spanish people and they were very loud at night. sometimes they woke me up at 3-6 in the morning on a school night. that is really annoying.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: it was really easy actually. I felt in the beginning like I always was lagging information. but afterwards I found out that it was because I didn't have to do anything so it was actually okay.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: i don't remember the exact progress, but I remember it wasn't complicated at all. they are all the time giving you information about the next thing you have to do.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: i had a koordinater on my host university who I could always contact, if I had any questions.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: you need to be ready for the registration. the registration starts on a specific day and time. when the registration start you need to be fast, because there are limited spots. if people only want 4 courses they will probably register for around 8-10 courses just to make sure. this mean that you can easily end up on the waiting list, but even though I was on the waiting list for all my courses I actually ended up getting them anyways. so don't be that nervous not to get the course right from the beginning.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I would recommend you to always read all emails carefully and be on top of the deadlines. it can easily seem overwhelming with all the things you need to do if you are doing them too late. this is especially incase something isn't working or if you are in doubt what to do. if you are doing things early you have the time to ask for help.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I think the level of the courses was the same as in Denmark. the school is only about 3 months so the syllabus seemed smaller than usual. however I still used quite some time on school. it was sometimes annoying, but im happy that I actually learned something on my exchange.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: the style of teaching was pretty much the same, besides we didn't have small classroom practice - which im used to in copenhagen.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
I took following courses 
10 ects advanced macroeconomics - master course (in Denmark: makroøkonomi 3)
9 ects advanced microeconomics - master course (in Denmark: valgfrit valgfag)
8 ects international trade - bachelor course (in Denmark: valgfrit valgfag)
5 ects behavioral economics - bachelor course (in Denmark: Behavioral economics)

I took courses with very high amount of ects to make sure that I only had to have 4 courses. im not sure if it really made it easier for me since the courses where demanding. they have courses that is only 3 ects.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would definitely recommend advanced macroeconomics and behavioral economics. 
macroeconomics was a really nice and structured subject. it gave me a lot of knowledge. behavioral economics was a really exciting subject, I learned a lot and it was easy. 
international trade was actually a nice course considering the syllabus, but the teacher was very boring and he used a lot of time on a lot of things that didn't really matter for the course. however it was quite easy to pass - I didn't give much effort to the class but I got a C anyhow. 
I would NOT recommend advanced microeconomics. its kinda similar to mikroøkonomi II in Denmark, but they are for some reason only focusing on some specific subjects. it was kinda hard to pass even though its multiple choice. there might be 1 correct answer, might be 2,3 or 4. it doesn't say in the task. but if you don't choose all the correct answers in each task you will get 0 points.

questions.question: Insurance DKK *
Housing DKK per month *
Books DKK per month *
Local transportation DKK per month *
Food DKK per month *
Personal spending DKK per month *
Communication (phone, internet, etc.) DKK per month *
Other fees DKK per month *
What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: no unexpected cost

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
food and drinks are SO cheap. half a liter of really nice czech beer cost 15 DKK. The clothes is a bit cheaper but most beauty products is the same. you can easily get a meal on a restaurant for 60 DKK. as a danish person with both SU and Erasmus money (approximately 500 euro per month) you will live like a king in Prague haha. 
Something that is really cheap is bolt. it cost 30 dansih crowns to get 7 km in the early morning when I was on my way home from the club.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: there is a lot of opportunities when it comes to bars, clubs, museum, escape room and other things. there is something going on every day. every monday is beerpong. Tuesday, Wednesday, thursday and sunday you get free tickets to a club called duplex. there is often planned a party friday and Saturday. in general there is a lot of social opportunities. for instance, I took a trip to Budapest with Erasmus in Prague.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: there is an organisation called esn. the organizes day trips around czech republic where you can see other czech cities. Erasmus in Prague also organize trips, both to other countries and they organize that people can go see a sport together and sometimes even do sports together.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
watch ice hockey 
visit Karlovy vary 
go to popocafe 
try a gourmet restaurant, its cheap 
try escape room - cheaper than Denmark 
try the horror and thrill park 
just have a walk in the city, it is a very beautiful place.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Prague is in Central Europe so it is pretty cheap to visit other countries. for instance I was visiting Berlin. it costed 20 euro for the bus and I paid 26 euro for 3 days in a very nice hostel.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: for me there wasn't much adjustment. the weather is really similar to Denmark besides it is raining less, which is nice. furthermore -5 degrees in Prague isn't as cold as -5 degrees in Denmark, since there isn't a lot of wind in Prague. The food is kinda similar, but I don't think they have as many healthy options as in Denmark.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: well in general its easy mostly to socialize with other exchange students and when I think about it I have never personally spoken with an exchange student in Denmark so maybe that's just how it is. I meet a few czech people. 3 at parties and 1 in advanced macroeconomics - we were making our assignments together. I will however recommend you to find friends from other nationalities. I had contact with other danish people, but my best friends in Prague is from ukraine, germany, turkey and others. it is really interesting to learn about other cultures. for instance, while I thought Prague was really cheap, my Ukrainian friend thought it was kind of expensive.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: for me I think czech people in general seem very rude. a lot of czech people do not speak English, so its hard to communicate and the get mad when you don't speak czech. if you are a girl I won't recommend you to take a bolt alone.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Prague is in general a beautiful city. I also enjoyed the prices since its so cheap so you don't have to worry about money. 3 months of public transportation is 37 danish crowns.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: im not sure if there is 3 specific things I wanna tell. just remember that even though 5 months may seem like a long time, then its going by so fast. remember always to get out and be social instead of regretting sitting at home. the first two weeks I was almost not even home, but in those two weeks I found my best friend in Prague. People are very friendly and open since you are all in same position.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: im not sure what it should be.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: it was definitely my personal growth. I got new friends, I learned more about myself and I got so close to another city. I feel so attached too Prague and I feel like its my second home. I would personally never move from Denmark, but if I had to, it should be to Prague.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: for me it was the low level og hygiene. te other students were disgusting if you ask me. in the dorm. people didn't wash their hands after the toilet. I even saw a girl going to the toilet, coming out, not washing her hands, and then she went directly to the kitchen and starting cooking her dinner. also I got a roommate from England who never cleaned her "side" of the room. even the first day we came I was surprised to see that the room was very dirty so I cleaned my own side of the room before I packed out my suitcase. my roomie on the other hand just packed out her stuff and placed it on top of the dirty desk and so on. she didn't clean her room ones. she didn't change her sheets for 3 months even though the dorm is washing them for you and you can get new ones ever 2 week. moreover she had old moulded things in the fridge including a 3 months old milk. I was probably really unlucky since I didn't here anyone experiencing anything like it, but still it was very challenging for me to live in.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: as I said, the dorm wash your sheets ev very 2 weeks, which is really nice. also there is a bar in the dorm where you can both drink alcohol, coffee, have food and more. they have som events every week, for instance karaoke. its a really nice place.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
